saints.name: St. Scholastica
saints.title: Virgin
saints.shortBlurb: The sister of St. Benedict, consecrated to God from her youth, whose last meeting with her brother won a storm from heaven by the force of her love…
biography: Born about 480 at Nursia in Umbria, Scholastica was the sister — by ancient tradition the twin — of Benedict, the father of Western monks. Consecrated to God from her earliest years, she at length settled at Plombariola, some five miles from Monte Cassino, where she led a community of nuns under her brother's guidance.

Gregory the Great relates in his Dialogues that brother and sister met once a year at a house outside the monastery for praise and holy conversation. At their last meeting she begged Benedict to stay the night; when he refused, she prayed, and a sudden storm of thunder and rain made his return impossible. 'She was able to do more,' Gregory writes, 'because she loved more.'

Three days later, from his cell, Benedict saw her soul rise to heaven in the form of a dove, and he had her body laid in the tomb he had prepared for himself at Monte Cassino. She died about the year 543. Honoured as the first Benedictine nun and the patron of Benedictine sisters, she is also invoked against storms, in memory of the tempest her prayer obtained.
saints.knownFor: Her holy life as St. Benedict’s sister.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 10 February
